Hi, I'm in the Pokémon TCG AI Battle simulation competition (username: dcallega). While downloading episode replays for analysis via the public API (kaggle competitions replay), I triggered a rate limit on the episode-replay endpoint. It's now been ~3 days and it hasn't cleared: I get HTTP 429 / "Too many requests" not only from the API but also when trying to view episode replays in the browser on the competition site. Could you help me understand:

  1. Is a multi-day cooldown expected here, or might my account be stuck?
  2. What are the intended rate limits for episode-replay downloads, so I can stay within them going forward?
  3. Is there a sanctioned way to bulk-access episodes for analysis? (I'm aware of and using the official daily pokemon-tcg-ai-battle-episodes-YYYY-MM-DD datasets.) I'm not trying to bypass any limits: I just want to view episodes again and respect the proper ones. Thanks!

I also met a similar situation when I participated in another competition (I crawled kaggle notebooks), and at that time it had remained for at least one year. I don't know whether the block has been finally unlocked because I have moved from my past place before unlocking.

The term must be case-dependent, but the extreme case it could be perma-ban.
Thank you! How would I know? Did anyone reach out saying your account caused any issues / violated some ToS? Anyone emailed or messaged you from Kaggle?
In my case there is no message or warning except the API error response.
